title: Dosing safety — paediatric & renal/hepatic adjustment (draft)
summary: Universal dosing-safety logic for weight-based paediatric dosing and dose adjustment in renal/hepatic impairment. Principle-level baseline; drug-specific dose tables are authored from public-domain sources (DailyMed/RxNorm) + national formularies during clinical review. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.
paediatricPrinciples: Dose by body weight (mg/kg) using current weight; use weight bands where the national protocol provides them.
Never exceed the equivalent adult maximum dose.
Double-check high-alert medicines (opioids, insulin, anticoagulants, chemotherapy, IV electrolytes) with an independent second check.
Use a neonatal-specific reference for neonates (postmenstrual age and weight matter).
Confirm the concentration/formulation before calculating volume to administer.
renalPrinciples: Estimate renal function (eGFR / creatinine clearance) before dosing renally-cleared drugs.
Adjust dose/interval for renally-eliminated drugs (e.g. aminoglycosides, many beta-lactams, vancomycin, DOACs).
Avoid or use with caution nephrotoxic combinations (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast, ACEi/ARB + diuretic in volume depletion).
Review and re-dose with changing renal function (AKI, recovery).
hepaticPrinciples: Use caution with hepatically-metabolised and hepatotoxic drugs in significant liver disease.
Avoid/limit drugs precipitating encephalopathy (sedatives) or bleeding in advanced disease.
Prefer agents with non-hepatic elimination where alternatives exist.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should attach drug-specific dose tables mapped to the national EML formulations.
